blocks.text: Screengrab from Asean PH 2026 MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Tuesday called for stronger regional cooperation to address cross-border threats, including online scams, as he opened the 21st East Asia Summit (EAS) in Manila. The EAS brings together Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) leaders and their eight dialogue partners including Australia, China, India, Japan, New Zealand, the Republic of Korea, Russia, and the United States. Marcos, speaking as the Asean chair, underscored the need for countries to work together against emerging challenges, noting that transnational threats increasingly move between physical and digital spaces. “At the same […]...
